newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bank to raise capital.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bank to raise capital.

text.p: Egypt's Mohandes Bank on Sunday invited existing shareholders to buy five million new shares to increase the bank's issued capital to 150 million pounds ($44.2 million) from 100 million.
The bank said in a published announcement shareholders could buy the equivalent of 50 percent of their holdings during the offer which would last for a month from July 7.
Bidders will pay the share's nominal value of 10 pounds, plus a premium of 2.5 pounds and an issue fee of 0.50 pounds, the bank said.
The share closed on the stock market on June 26 at 36.99 pounds.
The bank's extraordinary general assembly agreed earlier this year to raise the authorised capital to 300 million pounds from 100 million.
Mohandes Bank has a paid-up capital of 100 million pounds, some in dollars and some in pounds.

Results released at the end of the first three months of calendar 1997, the bank's financial year, showed that distributable profits were 15.149 million pounds. No comparative figures were available for the same period in the previous year.
The bank said on Sunday it made 68.21 million pounds of net profit during the whole of 1996, against 51.89 million in the previous year.
